t: Security is a process, not a product.
Amateurs hack systems, professionals hack people.
There are two types of companies: those that have been hacked, and those that don't yet know they've been hacked.
The only truly secure system is one that is powered off, cast in a block of concrete and sealed in a lead-lined room with armed guards — and even then I have my doubts.
Passwords are like underwear: don't let people see it, change it occasionally, and don't share it with strangers.
If you think technology can solve your security problems, then you don't understand the problems and you don't understand the technology.
A chain is only as strong as its weakest link.
Given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow.
Trust, but verify.
Never trust, always verify.
Complexity is the worst enemy of security.
The user is going to pick dancing pigs over security every time.
Encryption works. Properly implemented strong crypto systems are one of the few things that you can rely on.
It takes 20 years to build a reputation and a few minutes of cyber-incident to ruin it.
The weakest link in the security chain is the human element.
Data is a precious thing and will last longer than the systems themselves.
You can't defend everything, everywhere. The real skill is detect and respond.
The best way to keep a secret is to never have it in the first place.
Assume breach.
Security is always excessive until it's not enough.
Attackers only have to be right once. Defenders have to be right every time.
Don't roll your own crypto.
If you spend more on coffee than on IT security, you will be hacked.
Patch early, patch often.
There is no patch for human curiosity.
Privacy and security are two sides of the same coin.
The more you know, the more you realize how much you don't know.
Fix the problem, not the blame.
Backups are useless. Restores are priceless — test your restores.
A backup you have never restored is just a hope.
Defense in depth: no single control should be your only control.
Least privilege is not a restriction, it is a gift to your future self.
Logs you never read are just disk you pay for.
Security by obscurity is not security.
A secret known by two is no longer a secret.
Threat modeling is just asking: what could go wrong, and what will we do about it?
Shift left: the earlier you find a bug, the cheaper it is to fix.
Secure defaults protect the users who never change a setting — which is most of them.
The network is hostile. Design as if the attacker is already inside.
Every input is guilty until proven innocent.
Availability is a security property too.
Incident response is a muscle: if you never train it, it will fail when you need it.
The goal is not to be unbreakable. The goal is to make the attack more expensive than the reward.
Compliance is a floor, not a ceiling.
Rotate your secrets before someone else does it for you.
Multi-factor authentication is the cheapest insurance in security.
Assume every dependency can betray you, and plan accordingly.
You cannot protect what you cannot see. Inventory first.
Simplicity is a security feature.
The best time to think about security was at design. The second best time is now.
